outcome: Accuracy of ultrasonography (USG) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in diagnosing adherent placenta
Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and accuracy of USG and MRI
cohort: Thirty pregnant women with placenta previa or a history of previous cesarean sections
finding: MRI was more accurate than USG in diagnosing three types of adherent placenta, with sensitivities ranging from 92.9% to 100% and PPVs ranging from 93.8% to 100%.
